grammar.title: Prepositions of Time: In, On, At
grammar.explanation:
We use **in**, **on** and **at** to talk about time.

Use **at** for clock times. We go by coach **at** 9 o'clock, and the film starts **at** 8 pm.

Use **on** for days and dates. We travel by ferry **on** Monday, and my birthday is **on** 12 October.

Use **in** for months, years and seasons. We go by plane **in** July, and I was born **in** 1998.

Use **in** for parts of the day: **in** the morning, **in** the afternoon, **in** the evening. But say **at** night.

Do not use **in**, **on** or **at** before **next**, **last**, **this** or **every**. Say **next Friday**, not on next Friday.

practice.q: Rewrite with at: We go by plane at the time of noon.
practice.a: We go by plane at noon.

practice.q: Rewrite with on: We go by ferry on the day Monday.
practice.a: We go by ferry on Monday.

practice.q: Rewrite with in: Our trip is in the month of July.
Rewrite with no preposition: We travel on next Friday.
